A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TriDF and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–K. Corresponding material can be matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original TriDF evaluations, including visual and audio model results, specialist-detector comparisons, correlation analyses, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original visual and audio evaluations and reports numerical localization-hint results in its Table 9.

M1.justification: The synthesis and quality-control pipeline, human artifact annotation, question formats, artifact mapping, and scoring procedure remain unchanged. Revised task descriptions and model names do not establish procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same three modalities, 16 tasks, generators, and source datasets in Table 4. The revised text-to-human and image-to-video terminology clarifies existing coverage; changed question counts do not establish different tasks or populations.

E2.justification: v3 eliminates the entire evaluated specialist-detector comparison from v1 Table 9: FatFormer, AIDE, Co-Spy, D3, MM-Det, and DFD-FCG. It also removes InternLM-XComposer2.5 and mPLUG-Owl3-7B from Table 3, while adding FakeVLM to the perception comparison in Table 2. Removing the specialist comparison substantially narrows comparator coverage.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Appendix F revise the reported total from 76K to 65K questions, with open-ended questions changing from 29K to 18K. Appendix I.2 changes the stated correlation population from 26 to 22 models and explicitly introduces Net Benefit reporting. Zero-shot evaluation and 16-frame/default video sampling remain unchanged; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: Appendix I.2 and v3 Table 9 add numerical Benefit, Cost, Net Benefit, and rankings for 11 models, supporting the localization-hint analysis already discussed in v1 RQ2. The correlation plots, stratified curves, and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The correlation and stratification procedures remain the same; the revised model population is an evaluation-sample change.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises averages and rankings: GPT-5 video TFQ accuracy changes from 58.61% to 57.02%, despite unchanged component scores. FakeVLM perception results and numerical localization results are added; specialist-detector results and two Table 3 rows disappear. All retained Table 3 scores and the audio results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix I.2 explicitly defines Net Benefit as Benefit minus Cost, whereas v1 defines the constituent rates and discusses net gains informally. This is a limited mathematical formalization; Equations 1–5 and the other mathematical constructions remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and central claim: reliable detection requires accurate perception together with low hallucination. The scope of 16 manipulation types across three modalities is unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 removes the interpretation that specialist video detectors outperform MLLMs because of stronger temporal understanding. It adds interpretation of localization-hint net effects, narrows the blanket proprietary-model superiority statement, and corrects Claude's CHAIR description from 'low' to 'high' when describing worse hallucination.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-website pointer, specifies model variants more precisely, and revises dataset-license information, including FaceForensics++ and LRS2. Conversely, the acknowledgment no longer identifies NVIDIA NeMo and NIM as the deployment and benchmarking frameworks. No substantial new implementation or hardware specification is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for evaluated models, including Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5, and SALMONN, and adds introductory references such as ThinkFake. Some references associated with removed comparisons disappear. The related-work narrative and positioning around perception and hallucination evaluation remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites Appendix A task descriptions, removes a repetitive taxonomy paragraph, polishes terminology, shortens the Section 3 heading, and updates author and acknowledgment text. The main narrative and section hierarchy remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 move onto separate pages and gain revised grouping, citations, and notes. Table 9 is replaced with a differently structured localization table. Example figures are revised, several displays move, and Figure 10 is enlarged; the overall visual organization remains recognizable.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies previously missing numerical support for RQ2 and improves several averages, descriptions, and access details. However, it removes all specialist-detector comparisons, reducing context for judging detection accuracy. Unexplained revisions to question counts and the correlation population leave their relationship to the retained results unclear. These competing effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
